title: Brain MRI
what: Pictures of the brain taken in a magnetic field. There is no X-ray radiation. Sometimes contrast is given into a vein.
why: For frequent headaches, dizziness, seizures, memory or vision problems, after a head injury, and to follow a known condition.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes, longer with contrast
tell_doctor: A pacemaker, defibrillator, or other electronic implant
Metal in your body: joint replacements, plates, clips on blood vessels, or metal fragments
A hearing implant or an insulin pump
If you are afraid of closed spaces
If contrast is planned: kidney disease or allergy to contrast

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: At home, take off jewelry, piercings, and your watch. No metal is allowed in the scan room.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes with no metal: no zips, snaps, or underwire. You are often given a disposable gown.

prepare.title: Makeup
prepare.text: Do not wear mascara or glittery eye shadow. They can contain tiny bits of metal.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no special prep is needed. If contrast is planned, ask the clinic if you should not eat for 2 to 4 hours.

bring: Past MRI or CT scans and reports
Documents for any implants you have
steps: You leave your phone, keys, cards, and anything metal in a locker
You lie on the scanner table and get headphones or earplugs. The machine is noisy
Your head is placed in a coil. It looks like a helmet with a window
The table slides into the scanner tunnel
Lie still. The staff can talk to you over a speaker
You hold a call button. You can press it at any time
If contrast is needed, it is given into a vein during the scan
feel: Loud knocking and humming. This is normal
Sometimes slight warmth in the part of the body being scanned
If contrast is given, a cool feeling in the vein. It passes quickly
after: You can go back to your day straight away
The report is usually ready the same day or in 1 to 2 days
If you had contrast, drink more water that day, unless your doctor said not to
red_flags: After contrast: a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Can I have an MRI if I have metal in my body?
faq.a: Often yes, but the doctor decides. Tell them about any implant in advance and bring its documents.

faq.q: What if I am afraid of closed spaces?
faq.a: Say so when you book. An open scanner, an eye mask, or music can help. Sometimes the doctor gives a calming medicine.
There is no radiation. For most people, MRI is safe. The key is to tell the doctor honestly about any metal and implants.

reminders.text: MRI tomorrow. Take off jewelry and piercings at home and wear clothes with no metal. Bring past scans and implant documents.
